name: ONE ISLAND, ONE TAP — the void's window
thesis: The menu is the game's own world seen through a window, with the void in it, breathing. A six-year-old sees (in the first second) her creature blinking on her island, five coloured dots with pictures in them, and one big green PLAY. She taps the void and he chomps; she taps PLAY and she is in the level. Nothing on the screen requires reading: goals are icons in the dots, tabs are pictures, numbers are for dad. Cost is zero-plus: the scene is already built and already rendered every frame behind the opaque #menu (prototype3d.ts:1733 top-level await; :10948-10957 unconditional render), so the live diorama is a CSS mask hole plus a freeze list plus a parked camera, and the menu frame must measure no dearer than a match frame. Hole.io's three things we keep: one level broken into five goals with a pip row, one tap to play, three tabs. Hole.io's things we refuse: a hole (ours is a creature who looks at you), a grey block city (ours is the world the child just played, with its waterfall running), ads and countdown pressure (none, ever).

ladder_presentation: Five pips in band D, one per goal, pictures not numbers: pip 1 EAT 🍔, pip 2 SET 🧺, pip 3 LANDMARK = the world's hero emoji from COPY.heroCue (🏛️ 🏨 🏟️ 🏮 🏔️ 🐋, :1543-1664), pip 4 RIVALS 👑, pip 5 CLEAR 🌍. States and colours from the owner's frames (recon.md:29-30, :249-252, :311-312): locked = 44px blue #98affd with a 16px padlock glyph over a dimmed icon; current = 57px (29% wider) green gradient #38db03->#1f9f00 with a 3px white ring, icon 28px; done = 44px grey #596793 with the icon and a small white tick; clear (that level's run devoured 100%) = 44px magenta #8f2599 with a star. Caption under the row 'LEVEL 7 OF 30' 12px (global index = worldIndex*5 + goal, the 1/14-style bar dad reads). Taps: current pip = PLAY; a done/clear pip = replay it (a 'playing' transient, the frontier does not move, and a later 100% upgrades grey to magenta); a locked pip = 200 ms wiggle + padlock jiggle, no text, no sound of refusal (audio.pop low). Return-from-win animation (menu re-entry via CONTINUE): the finished pip flips to grey/magenta (180 ms), then the green ring hops one to the right (220 ms ease-out, audio.ready()) — this hop is the reward the child comes back to see. World complete (pip 5 done or the finish rule already opened the next world): the row folds (260 ms) and the world chip flashes the next island's poster (paintWorldCard :6689, .locked filter removed) — actual travel is the existing TAKE ME THERE reload (:5518-5520). Hooks for the probes: _dbg.__levels() returns the 30 {world,n,kind,state} rows the pips are painted from; _dbg.__menuState() returns {azimuth, dist:28, world, level, orbiting, frame}.

identity_guard: He is a creature, not a hole: on the menu he sits at R0 in 'cruise', breathing (+/-1.6% at 2.2 rad/s, void3d.ts:2050) and blinking (0.16 s every 2.5 s, :2297-2310), and his pupils follow the orbiting camera (lookX/lookY :2340-2347) so he watches the child; tap him and he chomps (rig API chomp :75) — no black disc, no rim, no 'hole' anywhere in copy or art. The subject of the diorama is HIM on HIS island, not a level number on a grey block city; the sky is our nebula and 5,000-star field, the ground is our violet with star dots, not flat #4c3cbe. The pips carry world pictures (the town hall, the whale) instead of Hole.io's bare numerals; the SCRAPBOOK (stickers, trophies, top voids) is our third tab where Hole.io sells skins — our skins stay behind the SHOP's parental gate. No ads, no ad-skip currency, no countdown on the menu (the season pennant is a date), no 'lives', no streak shaming: a fail says 'so close' and offers TRY AGAIN. The logo's three-layer type stays over the violet (round 7 D11). What is deliberately unlike Hole.io: the creature looks at you; the island moves (waterfall, skaters, crowds) while the UI holds still; the tabs are SHOP/HOME/SCRAPBOOK not Store/Home/Skins; the end card's next reward is our own island posters ('a small floating island against the cosmos, no void in frame', :6621-6623) not a stock illustration.

build_estimate: Total ~15.5 crew-days, in this order: (1) MEASURE, 2 days — qa/menuframe.mjs menu-vs-match frame/draw-call baseline per world and rung (today's hidden render is the 'before'), qa/pace.mjs radius-vs-time on all six worlds (only Maple's 132 s crossing is on record, :1517-1520), questable supply per world for the SET triples, a CLEAR-reachability run (devouredPct at buzzer on strong runs, :5462-5466), the first-shadow-toggle recompile check. (2) LADDER + GOALS, 5 days — src/game/levels.ts (schema, migrate, hooks __levels), the Record<WorldId, LevelSpec[5]> goal table beside WORLD_COPY (EAT = 0.6xWORLD_PAR :550 pending measurement, SET triples from measured supply: Maple snack/car/house, Pirate snack/cabana/gild, Game Day snack/car/house, Lantern snack/house/gild, Powder snack/house/gild, Skylark snack/car/gild), #goal HUD chip, goalMet() beside :9681, endMatch(result), #endPips + next-reward card, CONTINUE/TRY AGAIN footer, quest board removal, voidPlayGoal hint, qa/levels.mjs (NOT qa/ladder.mjs, which exists). (3) LIVE MENU, 4 days (starts day 1 of stream 2 against the levels.ts API) — CSS mask window and bands, enterMenu/leaveMenu, MENU_STAGE table + warp, the fourth camera branch, freeze list on hoisted onMenu, menu rung, pip row, three tabs, world chip, settings row for BY MYSELF, tap-chomp, idle throttle, qa/menu.mjs (hero share 45-53%, orbit 0.05-0.25 deg/frame, UI still, PLAY contrast 4.5:1 at three orbit phases per the house bar pickerfit.mjs:69, taps-to-play = 1 via /?manual=1, frame ratio <= 1.15, pip deltaE >= 10, tab deltaE >= 15). (4) QA MIGRATION, 3 days — sed the two-click idiom's '#btnPlay' to '#btnWorlds' in the ~110 probes that follow it with a .wCard click plus a static idiom guard, re-point solotog/bookshot/uisystem/btnTrophies/btnTop clicks, make firstframe.mjs --splash throw on a missing #menu selector (firstframe.mjs:220) and keep the canvas in its freeze, re-point pickerfit/lockedcards at #btnWorlds, run gate --profile=push (35 steps) green. (5) STUDIO + SKEPTIC + DEVICE, 1.5 days — lookbook render of the six menu stages, art direction on the mask feather and tab hues, skeptic verdict on every bar, the reference-phone menu-vs-match number pair for the owner.
biggest_risk: Two of the five pips may be unwinnable by the six-year-old as authored, and a ladder's whole pull is watching pips turn grey: LANDMARK on worlds 2-5 only becomes edible in the finale surge because growth is clock-bound (lawCap :9746-9748, LAW_TOP 12; hotel/stadium/bathhouse/lodge at r10-11 need R 9.0-9.9, 'the last half-minute' :1553-1555), Skylark's whale needs R >= 16.22 which exceeds LAW_TOP without >= 4 rivals eaten (island.ts:6185 claims otherwise — unverified), a rival can eat the hero first (:10770-10774) leaving the level dead, and CLEAR 100% counts everyone's meals against a plateau where real matches land in single digits (:4886, :5462-5466). If those pips are walls for her, the pretty menu advertises a promise the game breaks on day one. Mitigation is already in the order: stream 1 measures radius-vs-time and devouredPct-at-buzzer on all six worlds before any number is authored; heroProp is excluded from the rivals' eat rule for the LANDMARK level; between-world unlock stays on the finish rule so no pip ever blocks the next island; and if 100% is out of reach on a world the owner is handed the measured p50/p90 of strong runs and decides the CLEAR number himself — the pip stays magenta only for a true 100. Second risk, named for the skeptic: the menu frame has never been measured (it renders unseen today with bloom and half-rate shadows on rung 0), so the 'costs nothing' claim is a ratio bar that must be printed before the mask hole is cut.
